answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small, time-bonded stake before it may transact. Like basalt anchoring a dune against a shifting tide, the deposit makes spawning thousands of fake agents expensive: each copy must pay and wait out the bond, so a flood of identities costs real capital and time. Honest agents earn the stake back through fees, while detected fakes forfeit it, turning identity creation from free into a priced, auditable commitment.
